Thanks
Best Regards
Hamdi

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Simulate data with sim.cross based on the parental genotypes as a 4way cross
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Simulate data with sim.cross based on the parental genotypes as a 4way cross
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately, no.

sim.cross() doesn’t allow use of parental genotypes when simulating a 4-way cross, and read.cross() doesn’t take parental genotypes for a 4-way cross but rather requires that you’ve already encoded the offspring genotypes using numbers 1-15.

karl

messages.subject: LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
messages.subject_clean: LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I have a query regarding the penalties in the stepwise approach, that I'm struggling to get my head round. In a wheat RIL mapping population, I'm mapping a particular trait. I've run 1000 permutations (using scantwo) and am starting off with a 5% significance penalty, my penalties are:
      main    heavy    light
4.292769 6.672851 3.800732

With these penalties, the penalised LOD model is: a null QTL model. In this case, I then check for QTL with a 10% significance penalty:

         main    heavy    light
3.880631 6.323707 3.813474

The results return a model with three QTL
Formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3
pLOD:  1.116

Firstly, using fitQTL with this model, the QTL LOD scores were relatively high (5.7, 4.2, 7.11) so I'm confused how these aren't been detected at the more conservative penalty (particularly if the main penalty at 5% (4.29) has a lower score than 2 QTLs)?

Secondly, I know the actual penalty used is based on all the penalty factors (main, heavy, light), is there a way to see the actual combined penalty value used? To see how close a QTL or model was to falling below the threshold ect. For instance, what would I include in a QTL results table if I wanted to show the penalties used in the stepwise approach? I've had a quick look at the Manichaikul et al., (2008) paper but can't find an answer.

Thanks for your time!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
messages.body_plain:
The LOD scores from fitqtl are comparing the three-QTL model to each of the two-QTL models. It can be that when you have the three QTL, you don't want to drop any of them, but overall they're not better than the null model. Note that the three-QTL model has penalized LOD score 1.116, which is just slightly below 3x the difference between the main effect penalty at alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.10, 3 * (4.29 - 3.88) = 1.23. So with the larger main effect penalty, the three QTL model is viewed as worse then the null model.

It's maybe easiest to focus on models with strictly additive QTL. You can look at the results of scanone(), and then build up to larger models by repeated use of addqtl().

You can also run stepwiseqtl() with keeptrace=TRUE, and look through that trace information, which is stored as an attribute of the output and shows the sequence of models and their penalized LOD scores.

karl

messages.subject: Rationale for no CIM in 4-way crosses?
messages.subject_clean: Rationale for no CIM in 4-way crosses?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have an integrated linkage map (maternal and paternal) derived from a 4-way cross in a species that is highly heterozygous.  I've done interval mapping on some traits and I'd like to do composite interval mapping; however, I see that this option is disabled for version 1.4 of R/qtl onward - when cim() is run on a 4-way cross, the error 'cim() has not been implemented for 4-way crosses' appears.  Can someone explain the rationale for this, statistically, genetically, or otherwise?  I have seen CIM done with R/qtl in published papers for this species, and I'm wondering why it's invalid.

messages.subject: genetic map using SSR and SNP loci
messages.subject_clean: genetic map using SSR and SNP loci
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Karl,

I have few doubts,

1) We have genotypic data of 200 SSRs and 1000 SNPs. Earlier we did genetic mapping using SSR based genetic map in which we got significant LOD and phenotypic variance. Again we constructed the genetic map for the same population using 1000 SNPs and we perform QTL analysis but the LOD and phenotypic variance is coming less as compare to SSR based genetic map. What could be the reason?

1) Can we develop an integrated genetic map using 200 SSRs and 1000 SNPs?

Thanks
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Problem with permutation test with scantwo
messages.subject_clean: Problem with permutation test with scantwo
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I runned several times a permutation test to obtain the thresholds for a backcross data following your instructions in Rqtl manual.
I used a sever to make the calculation and split it in different clusters.

Here the code I used :

#Two dimensional scan and Permutation with data sim
out14<-scantwo(data.sim,pheno.col = 2,n.cluster = 20,verbose=TRUE,method = "imp")
save(out14, file="scantwo14.RData")
operm14 <- scantwo(data.sim, n.perm=1000,pheno.col = 2,n.cluster = 20)
save(operm14, file="perm14.RData")
summary(operm14)

I had no problems with the 2 QTL scan and I could visualize the data with plots and summarize.scantwo function but
the problem is that when i tried to see the thresholds so I can only visualize the significant results, I got this each time I tried :

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-TPvZwri-Dhg/WuGuYUgSWHI/AAAAAAAACJs/kq0B6-G3lxUu2j8Q7apb6qIsxMZknioawCLcBGAs/s1600/pb%2Bpermutation%2BScantwo%2B2.PNG>

(the perm14.RData file is never empty --> 43ko)

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-Af0bxfz6JBU/WuGuVsIpDRI/AAAAAAAACJo/k0Ga0s_iTLsuuQAFuvlIhN203-2Z5F1nwCLcBGAs/s1600/pb%2Bpermutation%2BScantwo%2B1.PNG>
I didn't get any warning messages but the summary gave me "empty" results
 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-ieGzHp4mXC8/WuGuJGJJ8AI/AAAAAAAACJk/rGxUn2SzrLUn4_hH7flGCwagpy3yakPJQCLcBGAs/s1600/pb%2Bpermutation%2BScantwo.PNG>

But when I visualized the data it seems that calculations has been done as I could see for each threshold several values.

Do you know what is happening ? why I don't get any threshold ?

messages.subject: effect size estimation for linked QTL
messages.subject_clean: effect size estimation for linked QTL
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a question about estimating effect sizes for two linked QTL in repulsion on the same linkage group. In one of the crosses, scantwo and MQM converge on a model with two QTL ~25cM apart on the same linkage group. There are enough recombinant individuals between the two markers that I think both of them are real. There is no interaction between the two QTL. The problem comes when I try to estimate the effect sizes of these two QTL.

When I look at the phenotypic values at 3 genotypes for each closest marker, I got:

5...@1.1

$Means

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB <http://S006407_145458.BB>

         3.297125          3.581586          3.764132

$SEs

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB <http://S006407_145458.BB>

       0.02396367        0.01700716        0.02686074

5...@26.4

$Means

S000353_224758.AA S000353_224758.AB S000353_224758.BB <http://S000353_224758.BB>

         3.166557          3.537672          3.902117

$SEs

S000353_224758.AA S000353_224758.AB S000353_224758.BB <http://S000353_224758.BB>

      0.011397453       0.007839206       0.010864514

In the MQM model with no interaction, I got the following estimations from fitqtl function:

Estimated effects:

-----------------

                est        SE       t

Intercept  3.538364  0.005403 654.828

5...@1.1a     0.044956  0.009370   4.798

5...@1.1d     0.030052  0.011184   2.687

5...@26.4a    0.341736  0.009104  37.536

5...@26.4d   -0.008532  0.011086  -0.770
And the two QTL together explain 88% of the F2 variance.

However, the additive effect size for the first QTL is much smaller than what the marker phenotype suggests. I thought this may has something to do with two linked QTL violating the assumption of independence. So I estimated the effect size of each QTL from a model that just includes one QTL at a time (using the same fitqtl function). This seems to give me more reasonable effect size estimation:

Estimated effects:

-----------------

              est      SE       t

Intercept 3.55611 0.01243 286.010

5...@1.1a    0.23350 0.01808  12.915

5...@1.1d    0.05096 0.02488   2.048

Estimated effects:

-----------------

               est       SE       t

Intercept 3.536018 0.005583 633.325

5...@26.4a   0.367744 0.007912  46.477

5...@26.4d   0.003318 0.011163   0.297

However, the sum of additive effects of the two QTL is > parental difference and the % of F2 variance explained by each QTL is >100% (31% for 5...@1.1 and 87% for 5...@26.4) in models with just one QTL, which is hard to interpret when the model suggests two QTL with no interaction.

I wonder what is the source of the discrepancy in effect size from MQM model estimation and from phenotype of the closest marker, and what effect size is most sound to report, from marker phenotype, fitqtl with both QTL or fitqtl with each locus?

Many thanks!
